item.text: {"question_id":"7B.2","answer":"For 2023, Tshisekedi’s correction and remedy record is mixed and attribution-limited. He publicly acknowledged that weak justice-system performance was a downside to his record and called for reform, and his government endorsed stronger ICC cooperation; these show some recognition of shortcomings but not completed remedies (BATCH-0028-E017; BATCH-0028-E018; BATCH-0019-E001). Presidential monitoring also acknowledged implementation difficulties for universal health coverage and free maternity care, while Tshisekedi acknowledged that economic improvements had not been sufficiently felt (BATCH-0020-E012; BATCH-0015-E004). The government announced investigations, arrests, prosecutions, convictions, and limited reparations after the Goma killings, and three officers were arrested after the May protest; however, these were government or military-justice actions, not clearly personal presidential corrections (BATCH-0002-E012; BATCH-0011-E021). The Goma record is substantially adverse: official casualty accounts shifted, no ballistic investigations or autopsies were conducted, victims and defense witnesses faced restrictions, prosecutions of civilians were found inadequately individualized, and many victims remained without effective remedy (BATCH-0011-E020; BATCH-0011-E021). Senior provincial commander Constant Ndima reportedly praised the operation and falsely claimed protesters attacked first, but the evidence does not establish that Tshisekedi personally ordered or approved those statements; Ndima disputed the account and claimed he ordered investigations (BATCH-0011-E022). Electoral observers documented major discrepancies and urged correction, while CENI reportedly declined independent audit offers; the supplied record does not show Tshisekedi personally correcting the record or accepting an independent audit (BATCH-0007-E010; BATCH-0013-E009). Release without charge and official investigations therefore cannot be treated as demonstrated correction, senior accountability, or victim remedy (BATCH-0003-E007; BATCH-0002-E012).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0011-E021"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0011-E022","BATCH-0007-E010","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0002-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence shows Tshisekedi personally correcting a specific false public claim, ordering a completed independent audit, or directly remedying victims.","Government, ministerial, CENI, military, and provincial conduct cannot automatically be attributed to Tshisekedi personally.","Some adverse findings are investigative or organizational assessments rather than final judicial determinations; casualty figures remain disputed.","The record does not establish whether Tshisekedi knew of, directed, approved, or later corrected Constant Ndima’s statements or conduct."],"corrections_made":["Removed the implication that releases, arrests, investigations, or ICC cooperation demonstrated completed presidential correction or remedy.","Added the shifting casualty accounts, absent ballistic investigations and autopsies, restricted testimony, flawed civilian prosecutions, and limited reparations.","Separated Tshisekedi’s personal admissions and endorsements from government-level and subordinate-official conduct.","Qualified electoral and Goma evidence where personal presidential attribution is not established."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A fuller judgment would benefit from direct evidence of Tshisekedi’s response to the Goma findings, electoral discrepancies, and journalist prosecutions.","The supplied material does not resolve whether later investigations produced authoritative findings, discipline of senior officials, or effective victim reparations."]}
